knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Local Area Scale Factor of a Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Consider a small rectangle $Δ$ whose bottom-left corner is located at the point $(2,1)$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane and whose area is $\delta A.$ Which of the following gives the best approximation for the area of the image of this rectangle under the action of the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}\log{\left(u - v \right)}\\- u^{2} + v\end{bmatrix}?
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant gives the local area scale factor of the transformation at that point:

$$
\text{Area}(T(Δ))\approx\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|\cdot\underbrace{\text{Area}(Δ)}_{\delta A}
$$

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\& =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{1}{u - v}&- \frac{1}{u - v}\\- 2 u&1\end{vmatrix}\\& =\left(\frac{1}{u - v}\right)\cdot (1)-\left(- \frac{1}{u - v}\right)\cdot (- 2 u)\\& =\frac{1-2u}{u-v}\\\left.\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|_{(2,1)} & =\left(- \frac{2 u - 1}{u - v}\right)\big|_{u=2,v=1}\\& =- \frac{2 (2) - 1}{- (1) + (2)}\\& =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(Δ)) & \approx|-3|\cdot\delta A\\ & =3\,\delta A.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Local Area Scale Factor of a Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Consider a small rectangle $Δ$ whose bottom-left corner is located at the point $(2,-1)$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane and whose area is $\delta A.$ Which of the following gives the best approximation for the area of the image of this rectangle under the action of the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}2 \left(u + v\right)^{2}\\2 \left(u - v\right)^{3}\end{bmatrix}?
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant gives the local area scale factor of the transformation at that point:

$$
\text{Area}(T(Δ))\approx\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|\cdot\underbrace{\text{Area}(Δ)}_{\delta A}
$$

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\& =\begin{vmatrix}4 \left(u + v\right)&4 \left(u + v\right)\\6 \left(u - v\right)^{2}&- 6 \left(u - v\right)^{2}\end{vmatrix}\\& =(4 \left(u + v\right))\cdot (- 6 \left(u - v\right)^{2})-(4 \left(u + v\right))\cdot (6 \left(u - v\right)^{2})\\& =- 48 u^{3} + 48 u^{2} v + 48 u v^{2} - 48 v^{3}\\& =- 48 \left(u - v\right)^{2} \left(u + v\right)\\\left.\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|_{(2,-1)} & =\left(- 48 \left(u - v\right)^{2} \left(u + v\right)\right)\big|_{u=2,v=-1}\\& =- 48 \left(- (-1) + (2)\right)^{2} \left((-1) + (2)\right)\\& =-432\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(Δ)) & \approx|-432|\cdot\delta A\\ & =432\,\delta A.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Local Area Scale Factor of a Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Consider a small rectangle $Δ$ whose bottom-left corner is located at the point $(2,-3)$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane and whose area is $\delta A.$ Which of the following gives the best approximation for the area of the image of this rectangle under the action of the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}3 u v^{3}\\2 u^{2} + 3 v^{2}\end{bmatrix}?
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant gives the local area scale factor of the transformation at that point:

$$
\text{Area}(T(Δ))\approx\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|\cdot\underbrace{\text{Area}(Δ)}_{\delta A}
$$

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\& =\begin{vmatrix}3 v^{3}&9 u v^{2}\\4 u&6 v\end{vmatrix}\\& =(3 v^{3})\cdot (6 v)-(9 u v^{2})\cdot (4 u)\\& =- 36 u^{2} v^{2} + 18 v^{4}\\& =- 18 v^{2} \left(2 u^{2} - v^{2}\right)\\\left.\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|_{(2,-3)} & =\left(- 18 v^{2} \left(2 u^{2} - v^{2}\right)\right)\big|_{u=2,v=-3}\\& =- 18 (-3)^{2} \left(- (-3)^{2} + 2 (2)^{2}\right)\\& =162\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(Δ)) & \approx|162|\cdot\delta A\\ & =162\,\delta A.\end{aligned}
$$
